title: Chapter 239: My Turn?
html:
“At first, I assumed she disliked my cooking, so I thought little of it. Soon, however, I realized something else was happening. Late one night, a noise from the kitchen woke me. I slipped silently out of bed.

“The house was dark, and I thought a thief had broken in. As I drew closer, I recognized my wife. She removed a large piece of meat from a plastic bag while holding a cleaver in her other hand.

“Chopping it would have made too much noise. Perhaps afraid of waking me, she merely scored the meat, seasoned it, and placed it whole in a pot.

“Was she making stew in the middle of the night? Perhaps she was preparing breakfast and lunch for the next day. I loved my wife. Though her behavior seemed strange, I did not disturb her. I returned to the bedroom and watched through the open door.

“The stew was ready around three in the morning. She looked over her shoulder and saw the open bedroom door, with me apparently asleep beyond it. As though unwilling to be observed, she closed the kitchen door.

“Then I heard her eating—wet, ravenous chomps. Twenty minutes later, my wife emerged carrying a large black garbage bag. The sight of her inexplicably frightened me.

“Her stomach was slightly distended, grease stained her face, and a satisfied smile curved her lips. After disposing of the bag, she bathed to remove the smell, then lay beside me as usual.

“The woman sleeping beside me had been hiding this habit. From that day onward, I realized I did not know her at all. I remained awake until morning. When I rose for work, my wife was still sleeping soundly.

“She looked just like Sleeping Beauty. It made me want to kiss her, but the things that had happened in the kitchen the previous night stopped me.

“Her stomach had returned to normal. Everything from the night before seemed like a dream. I dressed and went downstairs, but the rubbish bins had already been emptied, and the black bag was gone.

“The same thing happened the following night. She seemed afflicted by an uncontrollable hunger for meat. I stayed awake and watched her. At four in the morning, after my wife had fallen asleep, I dressed and went outside.

“I searched through the rubbish until I found the black bag. It contained bones scored with tooth marks—apparently those of a chicken. My wife had devoured an entire bird by herself. Once again, I realized how little I knew her.

“Another day began, but her strange behavior continued. I made a habit of searching her rubbish every night. The more I found, the colder my heart became.

“My wife appeared to be sampling different meats. At first, I found chicken and fish bones. Later, tufts of cat and dog fur clung to the bags.

“I loved animals. That was when I knew I had to confront her. She was either ill, or some demon had taken up residence in her stomach. No one could tolerate such behavior from the person sleeping beside them.

“At first, she denied everything. But when I produced the garbage bags, she knew she was cornered. She admitted she could not control herself. At night, an unbearable hunger consumed her; apart from that, she remained perfectly normal.

“She said that she would take good care of me and love me, but who would be willing to sleep with a crazy person?

“After agonizing over the decision, I filed for divorce, hoping to end the marriage quickly. My wife begged me to stay. I still loved her, but what she had done terrified me.

“I moved out and lived alone. My wife continued to love me. She called and messaged every day, pleading for me to return. Truthfully, apart from that one appetite, she was perfect—kind and fair, beautiful and gentle.

“Guilt slowly took root in my heart. About a month later, a stranger called. He identified himself as a police officer and said my wife might be connected to a disappearance at the radio station. He asked me several questions and warned me to be careful.

“I was grateful I had left her. Had I waited a few more days, I might have been the missing person. I returned to my rented room, reheated some cold leftovers, and ate quickly.

“After I was done, I swore that I was hallucinating. I saw my wife crawl out from underneath the bed.

“She smiled at me and said I had not changed. Even after everything, I still could not bear to waste leftovers.

“I did not know how she had entered my home, but I understood that I could never leave her again. I would become part of her forever.”

The woman’s story ended. No. 2 and Chen Ge instinctively edged away from her. She had narrated from the husband’s perspective, yet by the story’s conclusion, the husband was almost certainly dead.

The only living person who could know every detail was the wife. That wife was a radio host; No. 3 possessed a beautiful voice; and throughout the story, she had repeatedly idealized the woman.

The conclusion was obvious: No. 3 was the deranged meat-eater in her own tale.

“I haven’t heard such a wonderful story in a long time.” The man on the left applauded softly, his gaze lingering invasively on the woman. “All three newcomers have told fascinating tales. Choosing will be difficult.”

Then, he raised his head to look at Chen Ge. The eyes underneath the mask locked on Chen Ge’s face. “No. 4, it’s your turn now.”

“My turn at last?” Questions raced through Chen Ge’s mind. No. 3’s voice was distinctive enough to reveal her identity. She was Lychee, the late-night host at Jiujiang Radio. Chen Ge had even listened to her program before.

Everyone awaited Chen Ge’s story. He was, after all, the impossible fourth newcomer. Standing in the room’s corner, he concealed the blood twisting through his shadow. The crimson strands moved like needle and thread, slowly knitting a brilliant red dress.

“I have many stories. Let me think, which shall I share?”
